evidence.quote: The primary mission of ZYZZsat is to image the whole Great Barrier Reef in visible bands at 5 m resolution, so that bleaching is mapped directly
The operator is the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS), which already runs the long-term monitoring program for the reef
One satellite is therefore used. This also simplifies communications, reduces cost, and requires less time to build and launch.

criteria.reasoning: Mission, need, spacecraft count and users (operator AIMS; customers GBRMPA, CSIRO, BoM) all covered with reasoning and citations [1]-[6]. Rationale for direct bleaching detection is well argued. Minor: source [4] is vaguely cited (Nature news article).

evidence.quote: With a 4 m² sail the satellite re-enters about two years after the end of the mission.

criteria.reasoning: All major elements addressed with STK screenshots, access reports, hand calculations and file list. Checks verified: inclination, azimuth, period, aperture, decay rates (0.40 m/orbit, 2.2 km/yr; sail 5.8 m/orbit), data budget (115 Gbit → 29 Gbit vs 100 Gbit). Gaps: no X-band link budget (acknowledged); revisit estimate approximate; only one 60,000 km² strip/day is conservative.

evidence.quote: A 600 km sun-synchronous orbit at 97.79° inclination gives the same morning lighting on every pass, a 5 m image with a 60 km swath

criteria.reasoning: Conclusions are quantitative, drawn directly from the design sections, and include a candid limitations list (Vega C maturity, unproven fluid lensing at 5 m, ground-station equipment, 45-day mosaic). Slight improvement possible on recommendation detail.

evidence.quote: This report presents the design of ZYZZsat (Z-axis/Y-axis Zeroed Zoning Satellite), a single Earth observation microsatellite
Table 4: Orbital elements of ZYZZsat at the scenario epoch, 3 Feb 2025 00:00:00 UTCG (mean elements, J2000 frame).

criteria.reasoning: Clear structure, concise prose, well-captioned numbered figures/tables, executive summary, all references [1]-[15] cited in text. Deductions: vague references [4] and [15], Figure 2 generation method not stated, minor formatting/typographic slips (factor-of-ten expressions, unit style) and no table of figures.

technical_issues.issue: X-band link budget not performed; 50 Mbit/s downlink and ground-station sizing are asserted rather than demonstrated.

Imaging plan assumes only 60,000 km² per day (one 1,000 km strip), far below the satellite's actual capability; revisit/mosaic logic is therefore conservative but internally inconsistent with a pushbroom imager.

Revisit calculation (2,698 km / 560 km ≈ 5 days) ignores latitude convergence and assumes single-pass access; real coverage at 18°S uses ~2,570 km track spacing, giving ~4.6 days - acceptable but not stated.
Vega C status ('has not yet flown, first flight planned 2021') is accurate for 2020 but should be flagged as time-dependent; rideshare injection accuracy and exact release altitude are not specified.
Inclination-vs-altitude curve has no stated source or generation method (STK/MATLAB) and no data file reference.
Mount Pleasant is a VLBI/geodesy facility; addition of S/X-band hardware, licensing and cost are assumed rather than designed, with no elevation mask used in the access report.

overall: A strong, technically sound and well-evidenced preliminary design: launch, SSO orbit, elements, manoeuvres, ground segment, duration and drag-sail EOL are all covered with verified calculations, STK outputs and files. Main gaps are the missing X-band link budget, an over-conservative imaging plan, and a few vague references.
